evidence.quoted_text:
def claim_run_dir(self):
        base = Path(self.args.record_dir)
        resolved = base.resolve()
        root = self.root.resolve()
        require(resolved != root and root not in resolved.parents,
                "--record-dir must be outside the deployment checkout")
        base.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        require(not base.stat().st_mode & 0o077,
                "private record directory must have mode 0700: " + str(base))
        name = ("run-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
                + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
        self.run_dir = base / name
        self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
        return self.run_dir
evidence.reason: `claim_run_dir` creates a fresh `run-<timestamp>-<uuid>` entry under `base` and returns it without fsyncing the record base. The later durable receipt write fsyncs the run directory itself, but it cannot make the new directory entry durable in `base`; a crash or power loss can therefore lose the admission/recovery directory while the host remains held. The fix is to fsync `base` after `mkdir` (and the parent when the base is newly created) and refuse admission if that fails. This is an implementation defect in the durable recovery path, not a new requirement.
